n4aadd39cde2.s: Tilak's Home Rule League finally merged into:
o: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League
n4aadd39cde2.x: Tilak's League merged into Besant's All India Home Rule League, which in 1920 became the Swarajya Sabha under Gandhi and merged into the Congress.

na0b700e52ee.s: Which of the following came first?
na0b700e52ee.x: Tilak's League came in April 1916, Besant's in September 1916, the Lucknow Pact in December 1916 and the Montagu Declaration in August 1917.

n6c8ff4254a4.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
n6c8ff4254a4.x: The Chittagong Armoury Raid took place in April 1930, not 1929; the other pairs are correct.

n02a35ae7b80.s: Chandrashekhar Azad shot himself during a police encounter at:
n02a35ae7b80.x: Azad shot himself at Alfred Park after resisting capture; he was not executed in the Kakori or Lahore cases.

new.s: In which year was Lala Har Dayal arrested in the USA after founding the Ghadar Party?
new.x: Har Dayal founded the Ghadar Party in 1913 and was arrested in the USA in 1914.

new.s: After leaving the USA, Lala Har Dayal moved to Switzerland and Germany and joined the:
new.x: After his 1914 arrest in the USA, Har Dayal went to Switzerland and Germany and joined the Berlin effort.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Lala Har Dayal:
1. He belonged to the India House circle in London.
2. He was the first president of the Ghadar Party.
3. He was arrested in the USA in 1914.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Har Dayal was part of London's India House circle and was arrested in the USA in 1914. He was the Ghadar Party's secretary and moving spirit; its first president was Sohan Singh Bhakna.

new.s: The journal 'Talwar' was brought out from Berlin by:
new.x: Talwar (Talvar) was published from Berlin by Virendranath Chattopadhyay.

new.s: Muhammad Barkatullah published 'Islamic Fraternity' from:
new.x: Barkatullah brought out Islamic Fraternity from Tokyo.

new.s: The 'Swadesh Sevak' of Vancouver was associated with:
new.x: Swadesh Sevak, Vancouver, was run by G.D. (Guru Dutt) Kumar, not Bipin Chandra Pal.

new.s: The Komagata Maru began its voyage to Vancouver from:
new.x: The ship sailed from Hong Kong via Shanghai, Moji and Yokohama to Vancouver.

new.s: The police firing at Budge Budge on the returning Komagata Maru passengers took place on:
new.x: Police fired on the passengers at Budge Budge, near Calcutta, on 29 September 1914.

new.s: How many Indian passengers did the Komagata Maru carry in 1914?
new.x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 Indians, mainly Sikhs and Muslims.

new.s: The Ghadar Party grew out of which organisation in San Francisco?
new.x: The Ghadar Party grew out of the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association, San Francisco.

new.s: How many Ghadar leaders were hanged under the Defence of India Act after the failed 1915 revolt?
new.x: After the planned February 1915 revolt was betrayed, 45 leaders were hanged under the Defence of India Act.

new.s: Sohan Singh Bhakna called which Ghadarite his 'General'?
new.x: Sohan Singh Bhakna, the first president, called Kartar Singh Sarabha his 'General'.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ghadar Party:
1. It was founded on 21 April 1913.
2. Its first meeting was held in Oregon.
3. Its headquarters was at Vancouver.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The party was founded on 21 April 1913 with its first meeting in Oregon. Its headquarters was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco, not Vancouver.

new.s: The Paris Indian Society (1905) was founded by:
new.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama founded the Paris Indian Society in 1905; it was separate from Krishnavarma's India House.

new.s: The United India House at Seattle was associated with:
o: Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
new.x: United India House, Seattle, was run by Taraknath Das and G.D. Kumar.

new.s: Besides Germany and Turkey, the Provisional Government of India at Kabul was helped by the:
new.x: The Kabul government was backed by Germany and Turkey, with help from the Afghan Crown Prince.

new.s: Who was the Prime Minister of the Provisional Government of India set up at Kabul in 1915?
new.x: Maulana Barkatullah was Prime Minister; Raja Mahendra Pratap was President.

new.s: On 1 July 1909 in London, Madan Lal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie and:
new.x: Dhingra shot Sir William Curzon Wyllie and Cowasji Lalkaka in London on 1 July 1909.

new.s: Sir William Curzon Wyllie, shot by Madan Lal Dhingra, held which post?
o: Political ADC at the India Office
new.x: Curzon Wyllie was political ADC at the India Office in London.

new.s: The date of CPI's founding that the CPI itself recognises is:
new.x: The CPI recognises Kanpur, 26 December 1925; the CPI(M) recognises Tashkent, 1920.

new.s: Darsi Chenchayya, the only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party, belonged to:
new.x: Darsi Chenchayya of Kanigiri was the first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party.

new.s: Madame Bhikaji Cama came from which community?
new.x: Bhikaji Cama came from a rich Parsi family.

new.s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
new.x: Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur, 1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman President.

new.s: Sarojini Naidu presided over the INC session at:
new.x: Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur in 1925.

new.s: Nellie Sengupta became INC President in 1933 after the arrest of president-elect:
new.x: Nellie Sengupta presided at Calcutta in 1933 after Malaviya, the president-elect, was arrested.

new.s: In which year did the Surat Split take place?
new.x: The Surat Split between Moderates and Extremists happened in 1907 and was healed at Lucknow in 1916.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of the period:
1. The Komagata Maru incident preceded Gandhi's return from South Africa.
2. Besant's Home Rule League was founded before Tilak's.
3. The Montagu Declaration came after the Lucknow Pact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Komagata Maru (1914) preceded Gandhi's return (January 1915), and the Montagu Declaration (August 1917) followed the Lucknow Pact (December 1916). Tilak's League (April 1916) came before Besant's (September 1916).

new.s: 'At the Feet of the Master' was written by Annie Besant's protégé:
new.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, Besant's protégé, wrote At the Feet of the Master.

new.s: Annie Besant became President of the Theosophical Society in:
new.x: Besant joined the Theosophical Society in 1889, came to India in 1893 and became its President in 1907.

new.s: Which newspaper strongly backed the Home Rule Movement in Andhra?
new.x: Andhra Mata strongly supported Home Rule in Andhra (APPSC Group 2, 2017).

new.s: By 1917, how many Home Rule branches had been set up in Andhra?
new.x: Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917; about 200 was the figure for Besant's whole League.

new.s: The Home Rule-supporting paper Desamata was edited by:
new.x: Desamata was edited by Chilakamarti; Krishna Patrika was Mutnuri Krishna Rao's.

new.s: Who said, "The British Empire is rotten to the core, corrupt in every direction"?
new.x: The remark is Sister Nivedita's.

new.s: "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers", said of the Lucknow Pact, is attributed to:
new.x: Tilak, not Besant, made this remark on the Lucknow Pact.

new.s: Who gave the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
new.x: The slogan is Bal Gangadhar Tilak's.

new.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was negotiated mainly by:
new.x: Tilak and Jinnah were the key negotiators of the Lucknow Pact.

new.s: The headquarters of Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was at:
new.x: Besant's League was based at Adyar (Gokhale Hall), Madras; Tilak's was based at Poona.

new.s: Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916 at the Bombay Provincial Conference held at:
new.x: It was launched at Belgaum; the League was then based at Poona.

new.s: Who was the Secretary of Tilak's Home Rule League?
new.x: N.C. Kelkar was Secretary and Joseph Baptista President of Tilak's League; Arundale and Wadia were with Besant's.

new.s: Which popular title of Tilak means 'beloved of the people'?
new.x: Lokmanya was Tilak's popular title; 'Father of Indian Unrest' came from Valentine Chirol.

new.s: In 1914, Tilak was released from which jail after six years?
new.x: Tilak was released from Mandalay on 16 June 1914; his League came only in April 1916.

new.s: The Congress special session at Bombay (August 1918), which split over the Mont-Ford proposals, was presided over by:
new.x: Hasan Imam presided over the Bombay special session of August 1918.

new.s: Annie Besant was released from internment on:
new.x: Besant, interned on 15 June 1917, was released on 17 September 1917 under Congress-League pressure.

new.s: Which was the first Hindi newspaper (1826)?
new.x: Udant Martand, started on 30 May 1826 in Calcutta by Jugal Kishore Shukla, was the first Hindi newspaper.

new.s: Which of the following was sentenced to transportation for life, not hanged, in the Lahore Conspiracy Case?
new.x: Kishori Lal got transportation for life; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged.

new.s: The death sentence in the Lahore Conspiracy Case was pronounced in:
new.x: The tribunal passed the death sentence in October 1930; the hanging was on 23 March 1931.

new.s: The first Lahore Conspiracy Case (1915) related to the:
new.x: The 1915 case was the Ghadar case; Bhagat Singh's (1929-31) was the second.

new.s: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded in October 1924 at:
new.x: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in October 1924; the HSRA at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, in 1928.

new.s: The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' was written by:
new.x: Maulana Hasrat Mohani wrote 'Inquilab Zindabad'; Bhagat Singh made it popular.

new.s: What sentence did Batukeshwar Dutt receive in the Central Assembly bomb case?
new.x: B.K. Dutt was given transportation for life; he was not hanged.

new.s: Bhagat Singh was born on:
new.x: Bhagat Singh was born on 28 September 1907; 23 July 1906 is Azad's and 15 May 1907 Sukhdev's birth date.

new.s: Rajguru (Shivaram Hari) was born in 1908 at:
new.x: Rajguru was born at Khed, now Rajgurunagar, Maharashtra.

new.s: Chandrashekhar Azad died at Alfred Park on:
new.x: Azad shot himself in a police encounter at Alfred Park on 27 February 1931.

new.s: Sukhdev Thapar was born at Naughara in which district?
new.x: Sukhdev was born on 15 May 1907 at Naughara, Ludhiana.

new.s: Jatin Das died in Lahore jail after a hunger strike of how many days?
new.x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in September 1929.

new.s: Pritilata Waddedar led the raid on the:
new.x: Pritilata Waddedar led the raid on the Pahartali European Club and took cyanide.

new.s: Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate of:
new.x: In December 1931 Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate at Comilla.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the women of the Chittagong movement:
1. Pritilata Waddedar took cyanide.
2. Kalpana Dutt was hanged.
3. Bina Das fired at the Bengal Governor at her convocation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Pritilata took cyanide and Bina Das fired at the Governor in February 1932. Kalpana Dutt was sentenced to life, not hanged.

new.s: Ashfaqullah Khan was hanged in the Kakori case at:
new.x: Ashfaqullah Khan was hanged at Faizabad; Bismil at Gorakhpur, Lahiri at Gonda, Roshan Singh at Naini.

new.s: Rajendra Lahiri was hanged in December 1927 at:
new.x: Rajendra Lahiri was hanged at Gonda jail.

new.s: How many persons were arrested in the Kakori case?
new.x: 43 people were arrested; four of them were hanged in December 1927.

new.s: Trying to kill Charles Tegart in 1924, Gopinath Saha shot by mistake:
new.x: Gopinath Saha shot Ernest Day by mistake on 12 January 1924 in Calcutta.

new.s: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer in 1940 to avenge the:
new.x: O'Dwyer was Punjab's Lt. Governor at the time of Jallianwala Bagh; Udham Singh killed him in revenge.

new.s: Who fired the first shot at J.P. Saunders in Lahore in December 1928?
new.x: Rajguru fired first, then Bhagat Singh; Azad covered the retreat.

new.s: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Army in Madras (1933) is associated with:
new.x: Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary is linked with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army, Madras, 10 March 1933.

new.s: 'Bandi Jivan' was written by:
new.x: Bandi Jivan is Sachindranath Sanyal's work.

new.s: 'An Introduction to the Dreamland' was written by:
new.x: Bhagat Singh wrote An Introduction to the Dreamland.

new.s: The Indian Republican Army of Chittagong was founded by:
new.x: The Indian Republican Army was Surya Sen's group at Chittagong.

new.s: The Naujawan Bharat Sabha mainly aimed to rouse youth, peasants and workers and to:
new.x: It aimed to rouse youth, peasants and workers, oppose communalism and spread Marxist ideas.
